name: Fix Dashboard API Proxy Configuration
description: Fix or update API proxy routing in the cloud dashboard server. Use this when the dashboard is calling the wrong backend service.

incorrect_target.description: The current (incorrect) backend service being proxied to (e.g., 'IDENTITY_VESSEL_URL')

correct_target.description: The correct backend service that should be proxied to (e.g., 'USER_VESSEL_URL')

endpoint_pattern.description: The API endpoint pattern to fix (e.g., '/api/auth/*')

test_endpoint.description: A specific endpoint to test after the fix (e.g., '/api/auth/login')

tasks.description: Read the current dashboard server proxy configuration

prompt.template:
Read the dashboard server file to understand the current proxy routing:

File: repos/metabob-cloud-dashboard/src/index.ts

Look for the section that handles proxy routing for {{endpoint_pattern}}. Identify which backend service it's currently proxying to.

tasks.description: Verify the correct backend service exists and has the endpoints

prompt.template:
Check if the backend service {{correct_target}} exists and implements the required endpoints:

1. Look for the backend service in repos/ (e.g., repos/user-vessel)
2. Find the route handlers for {{endpoint_pattern}}
3. Verify the endpoints match what the dashboard expects

If the backend service doesn't exist, report this and ask for clarification.

tasks.description: Verify the backend service is deployed

prompt.template:
Check if {{correct_target}} is deployed:

1. Look in repos/deployment/helmfile.yaml or helmfile.yaml.gotmpl
2. Check repos/deployment/environments/production.canary.values.yaml
3. Verify the service has an image tag and is configured

Report the deployment status (deployed, not deployed, or needs update).

tasks.description: Update the proxy configuration to use the correct backend
Test the proxy configuration if dashboard is running locally

prompt.template:
If the dashboard is running locally, test the proxy:

1. Check if the dashboard server is running (check for process on port 3000)
2. If running, use curl to test {{test_endpoint}}
3. Verify it returns a valid response (not 404)
4. Check the response indicates it came from the correct backend

If not running locally, skip this task and note that deployment testing will be needed.

tasks.description: Document the fix in the audit report

success_criteria: Proxy configuration updated to use correct backend service
Backend service verified to exist and have required endpoints
